title: Request Skyline: prefix prioritizer, delta-stitching and residency crediting
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: When conversational workloads interleave many short, template-driven prompts and ad-hoc user edits, our GPU-resident KV slab ends up holding many low-value prefix fragments while cold-starting truly hot prefixes. This increases tail latency and memory churn during continuous batching.

Goal: Develop a runtime-level policy and light-weight data structures to prioritize which prefix fragments remain GPU-resident across requests (the "Request Skyline"), merge near-duplicate prefix deltas on the fly (delta-stitching), and provide a credit-based residency mechanism so we can amortize cold-start cost across similar requests without blowing slab budgets. The feature must be multi-tenant safe, low-overhead (<2us per request extra in fast path), and compatible with our existing KV fingerprinting layer.
acceptance_criteria: 99th percentile generation latency reduced by >=10% on conversational microburst trace (internal trace id: convo-mburst-2026-01)
GPU slab occupancy variance across ten-minute windows reduced by >=25% for mixed small/long contexts
Delta-stitching dedupe rate >= 18% on template-heavy workloads without increasing token compute by >2%
Feature gated behind runtime flag and rolloutable per-tenant via console
Unit and integration tests + benchmark harness added; PR reviewed and merged
implementation_notes: Introduce a compact per-prefix score (skyline_score) computed from: recent-hit-rate, size_in_tokens, tenant_priority, template_similarity heuristics
Maintain a lightweight probabilistic sketch (PCSA-like) per slab region to detect near-duplicate fragments quickly; sketches kept on CPU with Bloom filter fingerprints in GPU-resident metadata

Delta-stitching: on request arrival, probe slab's bloom + sketch. If candidate overlap > threshold, attempt to rebase request on the existing fragment and only append delta tokens to KV cache to save memory

Residency credits: each prefix accumulates credits when used in continuous-batching windows; credits are consumed to keep fragment pinned during eviction. Credits decay exponentially to avoid stale pins

Eviction integration: eviction thread will consider skyline_score and credits, and prefer evicting low-score fragments even if LRU suggests otherwise. When evicting, write compact checkpoints to CPU staging to enable fast rewarm on next similar request
Tenant isolation: use content-addressed encryption key material per-tenant for on-disk checkpoints; GPU metadata only stores fingerprint and skyline_score (no plaintext)
benchmark_results: Internal microburst trace (baseline runtime-1.21): 99p gen latency 285ms; with skyline alpha experiment: 251ms (12% improvement)
Memory churn on mixed trace: average slab churn drops from 2.1GB/5m to 1.5GB/5m
Delta-stitching dedupe observed 21% duplicate token avoidance on template-heavy test (n=120k requests)
CPU overhead: additional ~0.8us/request in hot path when bloom probe hits; worst-case rebase path adds ~1.3ms for KV patching (paid only on mismatch resolution)
rollout_plan: Feature gate behind runtime flag: runtime.kv.request_skyline
Canary rollout to 5% tenant traffic for 48 hours with extended tracing enabled
Observe 99p latency, slab eviction counts, and dedupe rate; if regressions -> auto-disable for that tenant
Progressively increase to 25% then 100% over two weeks if metrics stable
Console toggle added for Dedicated customers to opt in/out per-pool
decision_log: 2026-02-18: Chose probabilistic sketches + bloom fingerprint hybrid to keep GPU metadata compact (Marcus, Priya)
2026-02-23: Rejected full-content canonicalization due to CPU cost and cross-tenant leakage risk; instead use template-similarity score and delta-stitching (Ava, Sam)
2026-03-03: Set initial skyline_score weights: hit_rate 0.45, size_inv 0.25, tenant_priority 0.2, template_similarity 0.1 (experiment config)
2026-03-06: Agreed to checkpoint evicted fragments to encrypted CPU staging with retention 15m for quick rewarm (security sign-off not required for metadata-only storage)
